chapter: The craft of the ad lib player
title: Preferring to accompany, and Richard Davis
summary: His first violin recital, why he never wanted to solo, and his admiration for Richard Davis.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, I was a violinist, and I guess my first recital, I think I played 'Reve Angelique', and my name was called to go out on the stage -- church function. And I was reluctant to do so, and my mom pushed me out on the stage, and I never wanted to be a soloist.
But I kept playing the violin, and when I got to bass, I figured this fitted my personality better than anything else, and I always wanted to be an accompanist.
And that's where you felt comfortable.
What do you think about Richard Davis?

Beautiful, very -- he had been denied his talents long ago. He was of major symphony caliber, but he couldn't get a job, so he went his various ways of trying to find a spot for himself, which he has, for master musician, master bassist.

-- and then I can follow through.
